title: Stephen (Acts 6–7)
hookLine: the first to die for the faith, forgiving those who stoned him
last: THEY HELD ALL THINGS IN COMMON.

cards: Acts doesn't hide the arguments. One of the early ones was about food: the Greek-speaking widows complained they were being overlooked when the daily meals were handed out.
So the apostles asked the community to choose seven men to take charge of serving, and they laid hands on them. The first name on the list is Stephen.

In the Douay-Rheims: "And Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, did great wonders and signs among the people." He serves tables, and he also can't stop talking about Jesus. Within a chapter, that gets him killed.

teach.b: Some men from a synagogue in Jerusalem argue with Stephen and can't win, so they bring him before the council with charges against him.

Luke says everyone looking at him saw his face like the face of an angel. He gives a long speech, retelling Israel's whole story, from Abraham to Moses to the temple, and it ends hot. They're furious.
Then Stephen looks up and says he sees the heavens opened and Jesus standing at God's right hand. They rush him, drag him outside the city and stone him.

Luke adds a detail that will matter tomorrow: "the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul." Now listen to how Stephen dies. He prays: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
Then he kneels and cries out: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge." Those two prayers echo two things Jesus says on the cross in Luke: into thy hands, and forgive them.

teach.h: HE DIES THE WAY JESUS DIED.
teach.b: Stephen dies the way his teacher died. "And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord."
Martyr comes from the Greek martys, a witness, the kind who testifies in court.

teach.h: LORD, LAY NOT THIS SIN TO THEIR CHARGE.
teach.b: In time, for Christians, it came to mean a witness who gives their life. Tradition calls Stephen the first.
The Church keeps his feast on December twenty-sixth, the day after Christmas, and Catholics trace the order of deacons back to him and the other six.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Stephen, the first martyr, on 26 December, and ordain deacons, tracing their ministry of service back to Stephen and the seven.

games.q: you're Stephen, outside the city walls. the stones are coming. what are your last words?
o: a curse on those throwing them.
a prayer that this sin not be held against them.
a plea to be let go.
games.why: he kneels and cries out: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge." then he falls asleep in the Lord.

practice: Let a name come to mind, someone who hurt you, not the worst, just one that still stings.
You don't have to pretend it didn't happen; forgiving isn't saying it was fine, it's deciding not to keep holding the stone, so breathe out and picture setting it down.
If you pray, you can use Stephen's words for that person: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and if today it's too much, it's enough to want to.

wordCard.voice: Martyr. From the Greek for a witness in court: someone who testifies with their life. Tradition calls Stephen the first. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a witness, someone who testifies. from it, martyr.

carryVoice: Your line: lord, lay not this sin. He forgave with the stones still coming. That's seventy-five days.
